answer_core:
I would not give Marcus 15% equity, CTO title, and a board seat on Friday. That is too permanent before you know whether he reduces the company's dependency risk or becomes the center of it.

But I also would not make Friday a vague no. Treat it as a serious staged-partnership conversation: there may be a path to major upside, authority, and ownership, but only after evidence. The evidence should test platform delivery, revenue relevance, client continuity, team dependence, knowledge transfer, and governance behavior.

Keep middle structures alive without turning the discussion into an instrument catalog. The Friday stance is not bonus versus full equity; it is commitment after proof versus irreversible commitment before proof.

Use exit math only as a caution about false precision. Until buyer assumptions, departure scenarios, and platform value are tested, the numbers should not carry the ownership decision.

So the message is: I want to explore a serious path with you, but I cannot grant irreversible ownership and governance rights before we prove what the partnership does to the company.
